title: Considerations in Enlistment of Women for National Service and Current Proportion of Servicewomen in SAF and Senior Leadership
what_it_is: Considerations in Enlistment of Women for National Service and Current Proportion of Servicewomen in SAF and Senior Leadership

sections.label: Questions on SAF servicewomen
sections.summary: Questions ask about the proportion of servicewomen in the SAF, in senior leadership, measures to increase both, and considerations on enlisting women for National Service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Defence (a) what is the current proportion of servicewomen in the SAF; (b) what is the current proportion of SAF servicewomen in senior leadership; (c) what measures will be taken to increase the proportion of SAF servicewomen and SAF servicewomen in senior leadership and to expand the roles that can be held by SAF servicewomen.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Defence with regard to the enlistment of women for National Service (NS) (a) whether there are any other considerations apart from having adequate NS population to meet our national security and defence needs; and (b) if so, what are these other considerations.

sections.label: Conscription of women position
sections.summary: The Government's position on the conscription of women into military service remains today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Government's position on the conscription of women into military service remains today.

sections.label: Enlistment Act and women
sections.summary: The Enlistment Act as drafted allows both males and females to be enlisted and does not exclude women.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Enlistment Act to effect NS, as it was originally drafted and stands, allows for both males and females to be enlisted, the precise clause – a "person subject to this Act means a person who is a citizen of Singapore or a permanent resident thereof…" It does not exclude women.

sections.label: NS success with male conscripts
sections.summary: NS built a credible SAF with male conscripts, and in 1983 the SAF assessed it could cope with manpower shortage through efficiency and technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: NS has succeeded well enough in building a credible SAF with male conscripts, such that in 1983, when the topic of NS for women resurfaced, SAF's professional assessment then was "that the SAF could cope with the manpower shortage through various efficiency and technological means." Indeed, this is the case today.

sections.label: Uniformed servicewomen in SAF
sections.summary: There are more than 1,600 uniformed servicewomen in the SAF, making up about 8% of Regulars.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Today, we have more than 1,600 uniformed servicewomen in SAF who make up about 8% of our Regulars.

sections.label: Women in senior ranks
sections.summary: Women make up 5% of Regulars holding senior ranks of Lieutenant Colonel, Military Expert ME6, or Master Warrant Officer and above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Currently, women make up 5% of Regulars holding senior ranks of Lieutenant Colonel (LTC), Military Expert (ME) ME6, or Master Warrant Officer (MWO) and above.

sections.label: SAF servicewomen recruitment and retention
sections.summary: SAF set up the SAF Women Outreach Office in July 2020 to improve servicewomen recruitment and retention, and compulsory NS must serve national security and defence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Aside from career progression and opportunities in the workplace, SAF has also taken proactive steps to improve servicewomen recruitment and retention.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It set up the SAF Women Outreach Office (WOO) in July 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Compulsory NS comes with significant costs on enlistees and the society and can only be justified if it serves the critical need of national security and defence.

sections.label: No need to enlist women
sections.summary: Enlistment of males into SPF and SCDF is sufficient for homeland security, so women should not be enlisted for NS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Likewise, the enlistment of males into SPF and SCDF is sufficient for our homeland security needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: There is, currently, no need for us to enlist women for NS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We should not enlist women for NS to perform roles outside SAF, SPF or SCDF, even if that achieves some social good.

sections.label: Work near homes for servicemen
sections.summary: Because IT systems are separated from the grid for classification, work near homes was set up in northeast, southwest and central Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Instead of working from home – you cannot work from home because our IT systems are often, for classification purposes, separated from the grid – we have set up work near homes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, now, servicewomen and servicemen can go near their homes to a secure system and do their work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have set it up now over in northeast, southwest and central Singapore.
